extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting to top-tier computer science conferences; researchers studying peer review processes
extracted.subtask_description: Empirical criteria and measurable features for producing and evaluating author rebuttals in top-tier computer science conference peer review (ICLR-style rebuttal stage). Focuses on reviewer score changes, social/peer effects, and quantifiable author strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Successful rebuttal (INC definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A rebuttal is defined as successful if a review's final score increases after the rebuttal stage (s1 - s0 > 0). INC (s1 - s0 > 0) is treated as success (1); KEEP and DEC are treated as non-success (0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the primary binary outcome used throughout the paper; prediction and analysis treat INC as the success label.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal stage impact (borderline importance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rebuttal stage matters: changes in review and paper average scores before and after rebuttal significantly affect acceptance, and rebuttal primarily benefits borderline papers (initial paper average around 5.0–6.0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should prioritize rebuttal efforts for borderline submissions (initial average near decision boundary). The paper finds final score cut-off around 6.0 for acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signed social network balance (balanced vs unbalanced motifs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Model reviewer interactions using Signed Social Network Analysis (SSNA) and structural balance theory: four signed motifs (two labeled unbalanced, two balanced) capture peer influence among reviewers for a given paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure the number/proportion of balanced motifs per paper; an increase in balanced motifs after rebuttal is associated with reviewers moving toward agreement (and score changes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Positive link ratio (review sign ratio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign reviewer-review edges positive/negative based on score sign thresholds (e.g., ICLR scores: {1,3,5,6,8,10} with sign interval 5.0); compute the ratio of positive links in the reviewer network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive link ratio is typically below 50% in top CS conferences; changes in this ratio before/after rebuttal are informative about public/social pressures and acceptance control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-effect statistics of other reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: For a target review r on paper p, use detailed scores (Recommendation, Correctness, Technical Novelty & Significance, Empirical Novelty & Significance, Confidence) and compute statistics (max/min/mean/median/std) over other peer reviews for p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statistics capture peer pressure signals used to predict whether a reviewer will change their score; Gao et al. (2019) style aggregate features are strong predictors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of balanced and unbalanced motifs per reviewer/paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Count distinct balanced and unbalanced signed motifs (from the motif definitions) that involve each reviewer (or paper) as features representing peer influence strength.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including motif counts as features improves interpretability and prediction of score changes; paired t-tests show balanced motif proportion increases after rebuttal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer detailed scoring metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Per-reviewer detailed rubric items: Correctness; Technical Novelty and Significance; Empirical Novelty and Significance; Confidence; Recommendation score (1,3,5,6,8,10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation score correlates positively with correctness/novelty scores and negatively with confidence; these items are used in peer-effect features and analysis of score changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review-level activity: # reviewer replies (discussion engagement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of replies in the review thread (reviewer/author/rebuttal replies) indicating how actively the review/discussion engaged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Higher reply counts correlate with more active discussions; positive reviews tend to have more active discussion. Engagement can mediate score changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review text length (word count)
rubrics_metrics.description: Word count of the review text (and of author rebuttal responses) as a measure of effort/detail in review and response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negative reviews exhibited higher review word counts in this dataset; authors’ longer rebuttals (reply word count) are part of 'work hard' strategy metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review sentiment (automated sentiment score)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure review text sentiment with a fine-tuned DistilBERT model; output is a positive sentiment score in [0,1] (value < 0.5 indicates negative sentiment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sentiment correlates with recommendation: positive-recommendation reviews have higher sentiment scores. Sentiment can be an input feature for models predicting rebuttal success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper meta-information features
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper-level metadata used as features: number of authors; title word count; abstract word count; number of keywords; number of paper pages; number of revisions; has one-sentence summary; has supplementary material; has skilled author (previous ICLR pub); has top Computer Science scientists (D-index).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted papers tended to have more authors, more pages/revisions, and higher rates of skilled/top authors; meta-features alone are weak predictors of rebuttal success but relate to acceptance probability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply number (author response count)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of distinct replies the authors post in the rebuttal thread (a measure of engagement/effort).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treated as part of the 'work hard' strategy; used as a quantitative feature to test whether more replies are associated with score increases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply word count (author response length)
rubrics_metrics.description: Total word count of author rebuttal text (measuring how extensive the authors' responses are).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included as 'work hard' metric; longer rebuttals may signal effort/clarification but longer is not necessarily sufficient—targeted addressing of reviewer concerns matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text similarity between rebuttal and review (TF-IDF)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure of overlap/similarity between author response text and reviewer comment text using TF-IDF similarity metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to quantify whether authors explicitly address reviewers’ points; higher similarity indicates more targeted responses to reviewers’ concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text similarity between rebuttal and review (deep learning embeddings / SPECTER)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure of semantic similarity between rebuttal and review using deep-learning document embeddings (e.g., SPECTER or other DL encoders).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures semantic alignment beyond lexical overlap; used to quantify whether authors respond to reviewers substantively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Politeness in author response
rubrics_metrics.description: Politeness score or binary indicator for politeness in the author rebuttal text (authors being polite in tone and phrasing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being polite is advised as a strategy; politeness is measured and correlated with outcomes though the paper cautions statistical limitations in inferring causality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding references in rebuttal
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether authors add or cite references in the rebuttal (explicitly referencing prior work or evidence to address reviewer concerns).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding references is an explicit strategy tested in the analysis; it can strengthen technical claims or clarifications in the rebuttal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentioning other reviewers / building consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors explicitly reference other reviewers’ comments or attempt to build consensus among reviewers in the rebuttal text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 'make consensus' strategy can promote conformity among reviewers and is conceptually aligned with SSNA findings (balanced motifs encourage agreement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide more details in appendices
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors should include more technical details, experiments, or proofs in appendices (unlimited page allowance for appendices/citations) to strengthen the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While main-text upper limits exist, including strong appendices and more revisions/pages correlates with acceptance and provides material authors can reference in rebuttals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence of skilled authors / Matthew effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the paper has 'skillful authors' (previous ICLR publications) or authors listed among top Computer Science scientists (based on D-index); correlated with higher acceptance rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skilled or high-profile authors are associated with higher acceptance; the paper highlights this as the Matthew effect and recommends enlisting experienced co-authors where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring scale mapping to positive/negative
rubrics_metrics.description: For ICLR2022, reviewers select from {1, 3, 5, 6, 8, 10}; the authors treated scores 6, 8, 10 as positive and 1, 3, 5 as negative for analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mapping underlies sign assignment in SSNA and many analyses; sign interval choices matter for constructing positive/negative links.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine-learning prediction feature set
rubrics_metrics.description: Multifactor feature grouping used for predicting rebuttal success: Paper meta-information (Xm), Rebuttal text embeddings (Xt using SPECTER), Peer-effect features (Xp), Author strategy features (Xs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concatenate these feature groups and feed to an MLP for probability of rebuttal success; peer-effect features were most effective, and combining all features gave best performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer confidence negative correlation
rubrics_metrics.description: Observational finding: Confidence is negatively correlated with recommendation score in the dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use caution interpreting confidence; it may behave differently from other detailed scores and interacts with peer dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer behavior baseline: most reviewers keep scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Empirical observation that most reviewers do not change their initial scores; increases occur mainly at borderline scores while high-score items can show decreases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should set expectations: rebuttal can sway borderline reviews but many reviewers will not revise their scores.
